# EnterpriseGlue v0.25.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.24.2`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This release contains compatibility changes that require the upgrade guidance below.

## Highlights

- **identity-runtime:** Enforce explicit PostgreSQL tenant and narrowly scoped platform execution contexts, preserve identity and administrator workflows, deliver optional hash-bound configuration exclusively to the API, and surface authorized trusted-system navigation.
- **database-upgrade:** Adds a signed PostgreSQL schema-epoch bridge whose owner job stops before explicit-context enforcement while application startup verifies either side of the policy cutover.
- **managed-release-runtime:** Adds a durable, revision-fenced release effect cohort and a fail-closed inventory for proving whether retained API and worker effects have settled.
- **release-automation:** Prevents the advisory PR assistant from overwriting Release Please-owned titles and release classifications after generated release metadata changes.
- **release-automation:** Classifies generated Release Please pull requests from their changelog heading and advances the host chart from the current protected base.
- **release-automation:** Makes release-note preflight wait deterministically for the dedicated labeler to converge a regenerated breaking Release Please pull request.

## User and administrator impact

- Operators can configure platform identity bootstrap without sharing its credential with workers or database jobs.
- Pooled PostgreSQL workloads now fail closed when tenant or verified platform context is absent; deployment requires a coordinated security upgrade.
- Authorized root-scoped pages contributed by trusted system modules appear in the main Enterprise navigation on desktop and mobile.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Before migration 1700000000132, upgrade or drain every API, worker and retained-release consumer of the shared PostgreSQL schema. Older consumers cannot remain active against the new policies.
- Use the dedicated schema-owner migration transport and a restricted nonowning runtime role without role memberships; runtime startup rejects privileged application credentials.
- The apiConfigBundle chart delivery remains disabled by default and is separate from mandatory PostgreSQL policy enforcement. Qualify validate mode and restricted-role bootstrap before explicitly enabling apply mode.
- Preserve tenant and business identifiers. Do not compensate for an incomplete coordinated upgrade by disabling RLS, granting owner credentials or adding permissive policies.
- Deploy the independently signed bridge release and let its separately credentialed owner job apply exactly through migration 1700000000131 before starting bridge application replicas.
- For pooled PostgreSQL, set the chart profile to database.profile.databaseType=postgres and database.profile.tenancyMode=pooled; confirm the existing ledger is exactly the signed 132-entry inventory through migration 1700000000130.
- After verifying the candidate signature, source, backend/chart subjects, schema manifest, transition implementation and effect inventory, configure the release-effect cohort releaseId as the SHA-256 digest of those exact receipt bytes and use its projected inventory values; the chart orders owner migration, restricted preflight, and cohort opening before workloads.
- Keep the bridge and previous qualified release for the complete 28-day fallback interval; only the later owner-controlled release may apply migration 1700000000132.
- Run TypeORM migration AddReleaseEffectCohorts1700000000131 before enabling the release effect cohort API.
- Do not use a settlement result to terminate retained API or worker replicas until the response reports complete inventory coverage and settled=true.

## API and integration compatibility

- No REST endpoint or wire schema is changed. Existing verified identity, session, manual administrator and deactivation commands retain their authorization boundaries.
- The breaking impact is operational PostgreSQL enforcement, independently of the additive optional chart configuration.
- Adds release-controller-only open, close, read, and verify endpoints below /api/workloads/releases/{releaseId}/effect-cohorts/{cohortEpoch}.

## Configuration

- Host chart 0.1.20 to 0.1.21 adds optional apiConfigBundle with an existing ConfigMap key, exact SHA-256, validate/apply mode and one existing Secret key. The credential is exposed only as EG_CONFIG_BUNDLE_SECRET in the API container.
- Frontend-host 0.17.8 consumes trusted system-module main navigation from the owner-isolated extension registry, preserving declared root/tenant scope and authorization metadata while deduplicating legacy entries.
- The explicit postgres/pooled chart profile activates the signed bridge contract. Other adapters, single-tenancy PostgreSQL, and omitted profiles retain the existing database.migration.enabled behavior.
- No operator migration-skip or schema-epoch selector is added. The application verify role and owner migration ceiling are immutable signed manifest data.
- The managed chart pins DATABASE_TYPE and EG_TENANCY_MODE directly on owner, preflight, API and worker containers, so a missing or drifted ConfigMap cannot select a generic migration path.
- EG_TENANT_RELEASE_EFFECT_COHORT_EPOCH binds a managed release process to one positive effect-admission epoch. Managed pooled Cloud requires EG_TENANT_PLACEMENT_RELEASE_ID to be the sha256 digest of the exact verified signed candidate receipt bytes and rejects a release identity without an epoch; ordinary self-host installations may omit both values.

## Database migrations

- Migration: 1700000000132-enforce-explicit-postgres-context.
- PostgreSQL FORCE-RLS requires four canonical command policies per managed table. Owner-written catalog attestations bind source and parsed predicates, detecting same-name USING/WITH CHECK broadening, missing/stale attestations, and extra permissive policies; this is drift detection, not a signature against a schema owner.
- The TypeORM boundary serializes runner context, clears it on success and failure, and rejects unsafe reuse or privileged runtime identities.
- Runtime configuration reconciliation persists terminal task CAS and its receipt in one short transaction; external reconciliation remains outside the database transaction.
- Other database engines do not execute this PostgreSQL policy migration; PostgreSQL verification alone is not cross-database compatibility acceptance.
- The bridge owner entrypoint can execute the already introduced release-effect migration 1700000000131 but filters TypeORM before migration 1700000000132.
- The bridge accepts only exact migration-ledger inventories through 1700000000131 with the attested dual legacy-or-capability policy or through 1700000000132 with attested explicit-context policies.
- The owner accepts only the exact 1700000000130 predecessor or an already accepted epoch. Fresh databases and empty or partial ledgers require a separate signed bootstrap/recovery release.
- Migration: 1700000000131-add-release-effect-cohorts.
- The new deployment-global cohort table is managed through TypeORM and portable migration column helpers on every supported adapter.
- PostgreSQL pooled-tenancy qualification verifies that tenant RLS-hidden queues remain explicitly uncovered instead of being mistaken for an empty global drain.
- This workflow ownership correction does not change application data or migrations.
- This release-workflow correction does not change application data or migrations.
- This preflight-only correction does not change application data or migrations.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: no.

## Security

- The bundle is read-only, hash-verified and fail-closed with required secret preflight. No additional environment or volume is inherited by frontend, workers, migration, preflight or Plugin Manager.
- Platform operations use finite revocable capabilities after protocol or service authorization; global rows have no blanket null-tenant exception.
- Manual administrator grant/revoke cannot modify source-managed assignments. Password-verified recovery claims bind the complete existing membership snapshot and allow only an unchanged row.
- Baseline revocation requires the canonical inactive user locked in the deactivation transaction, including SCIM lifecycle paths.
- Application startup rejects apply mode for pooled PostgreSQL before schema repair, synchronization or connection-owned migration work.
- The bounded owner path cannot run synchronize, migration-ledger baselining, policy repair, critical-schema repair, generic grant refresh, RBAC seeding or legacy projection side effects; its optional configured-role action is limited to SELECT, INSERT, and UPDATE on the new 0131 cohort table.
- The signed candidate receipt binds the manifest checksum, exact minimum/accepted epochs, unsupported bootstrap/recovery states, 0131 owner-transition implementation digest, and exact release-effect inventory version/SHA-256; candidate image qualification verifies the same bytes and imports the owner, preflight, and cohort commands from the stable built shared-package layout.
- Application, migration, and membership-free preflight database Secrets are pairwise distinct; migration, preflight, and enabled cohort Kubernetes ServiceAccounts cannot alias one another.
- The existing timing-safe private release-controller credential protects every cohort operation.
- Opening and closing admission uses conditional revision fences, and verification cannot succeed while any inventoried source lacks authoritative coverage.
- No broad PostgreSQL bypass, direct tenant SQL, inferred receipt, or shortened durable-record retention is introduced.
- The guard relies on the repository-owned Release Please branch namespace and runs before any label or title mutation.
- Only an added breaking-change heading in the generated changelog patch is considered, and only for the repository's Release Please branch.
- Release preparation accepts only a generated release pull request targeting the protected main branch.
- Only a canonical breaking heading on a same-repository Release Please branch activates the convergence wait.
- Preflight continues to validate the actual release:breaking label rather than synthesizing a passing classification.

## Known limitations

- Kubernetes resource existence, secret availability and external provider registration require deployment acceptance; chart rendering and local signed-protocol fixtures are not a live consent journey.
- Pooled streaming and global identity/runtime queue continuations remain unsupported. Existing global task rows are not claimed as processed.
- Tenant queue cursors provide fairness only during a worker process lifetime; restart resets the cursor and this is not durable or cross-replica scheduling.
- Shared-engine readiness is a successful reconciliation snapshot. Later tenant lifecycle changes do not automatically invalidate that cached snapshot; request-time tenant authorization remains independent.
- Cloud rollout remains responsible for verifying the signed receipt and exact source/image/chart subjects before selecting the bridge; this OSS release does not implement a provider controller.
- The managed Helm bridge accepts only exact 1700000000130 upgrades and has no executable fresh pooled predecessor bootstrap; fresh or empty managed shards remain fail-closed and blocked pending a separate provider-owned bootstrap packet.
- Migration 1700000000131 is a bounded compatibility epoch, not final enforcement: its exact attested policy permits the released legacy tenant-context predicate OR the finite current capability predicate until migration 1700000000132 removes the legacy route.
- This foundational packet authoritatively covers tenant release assignment plus durable plugin event and fixed-schedule work only; runtime membership, engine mutations, Git writes, email and diagnostic delivery, tenant secret broker mutations, plugin gateway calls, configuration reconciliation, and other enumerated sources keep the overall settlement result fail-closed until later packets instrument them.
- A cohort epoch must be configured before effects are admitted; a cohort opened after untracked work began is not eligible for shutdown proof. The epoch is immutable for a release identity because covered work rows are release-bound rather than epoch-tagged.
- The PR assistant remains advisory for generated release pull requests; the dedicated release labeler owns their classification.
- Manual pull requests continue to use title, checked checklist, or BREAKING-CHANGE declaration classification.
- Ordinary pull requests still rely exclusively on their explicit release label and conventional metadata.

## Rollback

- There is no in-place PostgreSQL down migration restoring permissive policies. Rollback requires the qualified pre-upgrade backup and compatible runtime; restoring that backup loses subsequent writes.
- Disabling optional chart delivery removes the API mount and secret environment but does not undo persisted provider configuration or mandatory policy enforcement.
- Before migration 1700000000132, a qualified v0.24.2 predecessor may overlap migration 1700000000131 only with EG_DATABASE_STARTUP_MODE=verify; its apply path would recreate the legacy policy and invalidate the exact dual attestation. Database rollback still uses the qualified pre-upgrade backup.
- After migration 1700000000132, use the qualified pre-upgrade backup and compatible runtime; do not edit the TypeORM ledger or recreate permissive policies in place.
- Stop using the cohort endpoints, unset EG_TENANT_RELEASE_EFFECT_COHORT_EPOCH, deploy the previous host packages, then run the migration down only after confirming no operator depends on retained cohort history.
- Revert the ownership guard and contract test, then manually normalize generated release pull request labels after every metadata refresh.
- Revert the labeler, chart preparation, and contract-test changes; manually label and correct any affected generated release pull request before protected checks.
- Revert the preflight derivation and contract test, then rerun failed preflight workflows after generated release labels converge.
